groups.Dynamics: Controls loudness and sustain, or silences noise between notes. Use compression for even picking and a gate for quiet pauses.
groups.Distortion: Adds grit, sustain and harmonics. Use low drive for a gentle push, or higher drive for thick riffs and singing leads.
groups.Modulation: Moves the sound with repeating changes in pitch, phase or volume. Use slow movement for texture and faster movement for a strong pulse.
groups.Delay: Repeats notes after a short wait. Use short repeats for extra body, tempo sync for rhythmic patterns, or longer repeats for spacious leads.
groups.Reverb: Adds a sense of room and distance around the notes. Use a little for natural space or a long tail for ambient parts.
groups.Filter: Emphasizes a moving band of frequencies for vowel-like or synth textures. Try it on single-note grooves and expressive rhythmic parts.
groups.Pitch: Adds shifted notes or harmonies. Use octaves for weight, a small shift for width, or an expression pedal for sweeping pitch bends.
groups.Preamp+EQ: Shapes frequency balance and signal level. Use it to remove muddiness, bring out attack or balance two different sounds.
groups.Volume/Pan: Changes loudness or the stereo position. Assign an expression pedal for volume swells or to move the sound between left and right.
groups.Wah: Sweeps a resonant filter to make notes speak. Assign Position to an expression pedal for classic wah phrases or park it for a focused tone.
groups.FX Loop: Routes the signal through external effects connected to the pedal. Match send and return levels, then choose how much returned sound to blend.

amps.clean: Open, clear attack with room for playing dynamics. Start with low Drive for clean chords, then raise it for edge-of-breakup blues.
amps.crunch: Touch-sensitive grit with a strong midrange. Try it for rock rhythm, blues leads and tones that clean up when you play softly.
amps.highGain: Dense saturation and sustained notes. Use it for heavy riffs and leads; reduce bass or drive if fast chords lose definition.
amps.bass: Full low end with a firm note foundation. Try it for bass lines or rounded guitar textures, keeping enough mids for definition.
amps.acoustic: A lighter, more open voice for acoustic-style parts. Keep Drive low and adjust the tone controls for clear strumming.
amps.preamp: This variant models the preamp section. Try it when another amplifier supplies the power-amp character.

cabs.single: One speaker gives a focused, compact voice. Try it for clear small-combo tones and intimate recording sounds.
cabs.dual: Two speakers add breadth while retaining a clear attack. Try it for open chords and balanced clean or crunch tones.
cabs.quad: A larger speaker array gives a broad, weighty cabinet voice. Try it for rock riffs and a strong low-mid foundation.
cabs.none: Passes the amp sound without a cabinet model. Try it when a physical guitar cabinet supplies the speaker sound.

mics.dynamic: A focused microphone voice that brings out attack and midrange. Try it when guitars need to cut through a busy mix.
mics.ribbon: A rounded microphone voice with a softer top end. Try it to smooth bright cabinets or add body to driven sounds.
mics.condenser: A detailed microphone voice with an open top end. Try it for clean passages and a more spacious cabinet sound.
mics.offAxis: Off-axis placement softens the brightest part of the speaker tone.
